title: Scalar pasting for twisted pullback composition and iterated purity
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Their composite $gf=g\circ f$ has pure relative dimension $d+e$ [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. For $R=E,L$, use $\mathcal C_R(W)=D^b_c(W,R)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $T_W=T_{L/E,W}$ for scalar extension [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. For $h=f,g,gf$ put $H_{h,R}=Lh_R^*(-)(d_h)[2d_h]$ and $G_{h,R}=Rh_R^!$, with $d_f=d,d_g=e,d_{gf}=d+e$. Use the rationalizations $\gamma_{h,R}:H_{h,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,R}$ of the simultaneous integral purity family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], as in [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Let $a_{h,M}:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}H_{h,E}M\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{h,L}T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}M$ and $b_{h,M}:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}G_{h,E}M\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,L}T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}M$ be the rationalized comparisons in that integral statement; $b$ is the specified adjoint transpose of the inverse compact-support coefficient comparison followed by the scalar-extended counit. Let $u^R_K:H_{gf,R}K\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{f,R}H_{g,R}K$ be the canonical pullback-composition, twist-addition and shift comparison. Set $q^R_K=\gamma_{f,R,G_{g,R}K}\circ H_{f,R}(\gamma_{g,R,K})$.

For $K\in\mathcal C_E(Z)$ define
$$A_K=H_{f,L}(a_{g,K})\circ a_{f,H_{g,E}K},\qquad \beta_K=G_{f,L}(b_{g,K})\circ b_{f,G_{g,E}K}.$$
Then the canonical twisted pullback compositor and the horizontally composed purity transformation satisfy
$$A_K\circ T_X(u^E_K)=u^L_{T_ZK}\circ a_{gf,K},$$
$$\beta_K\circ T_X(q^E_K)=q^L_{T_ZK}\circ A_K.$$
The first equality is between maps from $T_XH_{gf,E}K$ to $H_{f,L}H_{g,L}T_ZK$; the second is between maps from $T_XH_{f,E}H_{g,E}K$ to $G_{f,L}G_{g,L}T_ZK$. Both hold naturally in $K$, with the identity-extension, successive coefficient-extension tensor-associator and shift identifications specified for $a,b$ in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] and for $T$ in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

proof.text: For family_existsUnique, extract the shift, source localization, purity isomorphism and source scalar isomorphisms from lem-pur-rational-scalar-comparison-identification. Prove uniqueness separately: good complexes localize essentially surjectively by lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, so evaluate SourceLocalizationNormalization on one good resolution of each integral pullback and cancel sourceObjectIdentification. Every raw rational object has an integral finite-Tor representative by lem-coef-integral-residue-tor; invertibility of the coefficient prime in residue fields is furnished by lem-weil-compact-support-normalized-scalar-isomorphisms. Cancel the common source localization in gamma_localization on those representatives to identify gamma. The a_normalization equations identify all a components. Compare the two localization shift squares on each integral representative, cancel the localization and qYShift factors, and obtain equality of every shift natural isomorphism. Function extensionality, structure extensionality and proof irrelevance conclude uniqueness. This Lean proof is complete; the following eight steps remain the plan for iteratedPurityScalarPasting.

Use [lem-pur-rational-normalized-purity-diagrams] for the domains and the rationalized natural comparisons, not for the desired pasting equations. Every integral representative lies in the uniform finite-Tor domain; all intermediate $H$ and $G$ expressions and their comparison maps are therefore defined. Its single-morphism equation gives, for $h=f,g,gf$ and any input $M$,
$$b_{h,M}T(\gamma_{h,E,M})=\gamma_{h,L,TM}a_{h,M}.$$
It also gives naturality in $M$ and the stated unit, successive-extension and shift laws for these very $a,b$. No comparison with a separately chosen purity family or exceptional scalar map is made.

proof.text:
Write $P_{h,R}=Lh_R^*$ for the completed pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] occurring in $H_{h,R}$, $v^R:P_{gf,R}\to P_{f,R}P_{g,R}$ for its canonical compositor, and $p_h:TP_{h,E}\to P_{h,L}T$ for the pullback constituent of $a$. Apply [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] with $h=f$, $k=g$. Its specified pullback scalar comparisons are the choices of the comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] from which $a$ is built, for the strict-tower scalar extension, and its compositor $c^E$ is the limit of the termwise finite composition maps, which [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] identifies with the canonical compositor $v^E$; likewise for $L$. It gives, as an equality of whole quotient diagrams before realization and then after rationalization,
$$P_{f,L}(p_{g,K})p_{f,P_{g,E}K}T_X(v^E_K)=v^L_{T_ZK}p_{gf,K}.$$
By [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], $a$ is expressed for the ordinary derived-tensor presentation $C=T$ (before rationalization) through the natural completion isomorphism $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Replacing every strict-tower extension by $C$ conjugates both sides by $\chi$; by naturality of $\chi$ the inner $\chi$ factors cancel, so the equation holds for the constituents of $a$ and the $T$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The pullback comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] belong to the PBC completed pullback, a different functor, and are not used. That proposition is used only for $T$. Its hypotheses hold: separated finite-type $k$-schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $\ell$ is invertible on them since $\ell\ne p$.

proof.text: The tensor/pullback constituents can be combined with the coefficient comparisons on the specified completed models. Indeed [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] gives both the monoidality equation for a composite pullback and the scalar square for its tensor comparison, including inverses. At a quotient level its scalar square sends a generalized tensor $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ on either route to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. Thus it remains the same equality after any tensor reassociation. [lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization] identifies the actual completed scalar comparisons with the total-limit images of these whole-system maps. [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] identifies the tensor associators, symmetry and pullback compositor, including substitution into a larger expression, with their whole-system counterparts. Apply the limit functor to the equality and conjugate by those natural identifications; this proves equality for the actual completed maps. Rationalization preserves this equality. This uses equality in the derived category of whole systems before the limit, never detection of an integral equality by individual reductions. The comparisons of [lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization] are those of the strict-tower scalar extension. Conjugation by the natural completion isomorphism $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], through which $a$ and $T$ are expressed, carries the equality to that ordinary derived-tensor presentation, since each inner $\chi$ cancels against its inverse by naturality.

proof.text:
Check the Tate-line constituents explicitly. The first-twist pullback sends an inverse-image root system to its pulled-back root system, with coefficients unchanged; its coefficient square is clause 4 of [lem-pur-integral-twist-line-inverse-image]. The scalar maps on powers are the tensor-power maps of [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change]. The recursively associated nonnegative powers therefore send
$$(l_1\otimes\cdots\otimes l_{d+e})\otimes b\ \longmapsto\ (l_{d+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes l_{d+e}\otimes1)\otimes(l_1\otimes\cdots\otimes l_d\otimes b)$$
on both routes after splitting into the ordered blocks $e,d$. In this formula the symbols in the output are understood in the scalar-extended lines; moving $b$ to either block is the balanced tensor relation. The zero block is the coefficient unit. For the recursion, the zero case is scalar multiplication, the one case is the first-line square, and each successor is that square tensored with the preceding case followed by the tensor comparison. Its compatibility with reassociation and block symmetry is exactly the cochain coherence of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Pulling a root system first along $g$ and then along $f$ gives the same system as along $gf$; this also proves the composition law for the line maps. These are statements about the specified tensor/roots maps, so the realization identifications of Step 3 apply to their composites.

proof.text: There is no omitted shift sign in the preceding squares. By [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints], on K-flat representatives the tensor-shift comparison $K[r]\otimes L[s]\to(K\otimes L)[r+s]$ multiplies the degree-$i$ summand by $(-1)^{si}$, and symmetry has sign $(-1)^{ij}$. Every shifted Tate block here has an even shift $2d$ or $2e$ and its unshifted line has degree zero. Consequently all signs introduced by moving these blocks are $1$, including $(-1)^{(2d)(2e)}$. Tensor reassociation is unsigned. Coefficient extension acts in degree zero, so it commutes termwise with these reindexings. [lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift], whose quotient-tensor comparison $b_P$ is the chain-level form of the completion isomorphism $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], identifies that termwise comparison with the specified completed scalar shift on the Roos cone; its second-coordinate sign $(-1)^{2d}$ or $(-1)^{2e}$ is also $1$. The same calculation with an additional input shift by $1$ has the same sign on both sides because the Tate shifts remain even. Thus the equations are compatible with the canonical input shift as well.

proof.text:
Expand $u$ into its canonical factors: shift reassociation, pullback composition and the ordered twist splitting, tensor reassociation, inverse Tate pullback in the $e$ block, inverse tensor-pullback comparison, the two inverse shift reassociations, and the intermediate realization unit. This is the finite-level prescription of [def-pur-composition-comparisons]; [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] gives its specified completed realization. The geometric pullback factor commutes with scalars by Step 2, the tensor factors by Step 3, the line splitting and pullback factors by Step 4, and the shift factors by Step 5. Inverse factors commute as well, by multiplying each square by its two inverses. Paste these squares in the displayed order. Internal scalar comparisons cancel in consecutive squares; the initial vertical arrow is $a_{gf,K}$ and the final vertical arrow is $H_{f,L}(a_{g,K})a_{f,H_{g,E}K}=A_K$. The resulting boundary equation is
$$A_KT_X(u^E_K)=u^L_{T_ZK}a_{gf,K}.$$
This is a calculation for the canonical $u$, not an endpoint isomorphism chosen using purity.

proof.text:
Suppress coefficient and object subscripts only in this calculation; every $T$ is on the displayed output scheme. Expand $\beta$ and $q$ and use the $f$-purity square of Step 1 at $G_{g,E}K$. Naturality of $a_f$ at $\gamma_{g,E,K}$ then gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta T(q^E)
&=G_{f,L}(b_g)\gamma_{f,L,T_YG_{g,E}K}a_{f,G_{g,E}K}T_XH_{f,E}(\gamma_{g,E,K})\\
&=G_{f,L}(b_g)\gamma_{f,L,T_YG_{g,E}K}H_{f,L}(T_Y\gamma_{g,E,K})a_{f,H_{g,E}K}.
\end{aligned}$$
Naturality of $\gamma_{f,L}$ at $b_{g,K}:T_YG_{g,E}K\to G_{g,L}T_ZK$ moves $G_{f,L}(b_g)$ to the right as $H_{f,L}(b_g)$. Apply the $g$-purity square of Step 1 inside $H_{f,L}$. The last expression is
$$\gamma_{f,L,G_{g,L}T_ZK}H_{f,L}(\gamma_{g,L,T_ZK})H_{f,L}(a_{g,K})a_{f,H_{g,E}K}=q^L_{T_ZK}A_K.$$
All uses of naturality and both purity squares are supplied by [lem-pur-rational-normalized-purity-diagrams]. Functoriality and associativity justify the regrouping, so this proves the second equation with exactly the stated source and target.

proof.text: Finally all constructions above are natural in $K$, so the component equalities are natural-transformation equalities. For successive coefficient extensions, denote a comparison for a functor $F$ by $w_F:T F_E\to F_L T$. Horizontal composition is $w_{FG}=F_L(w_G)w_FG_E$; substitute the two tower equations for $w_F,w_G$, and use naturality of $w_F$ at $w_G$ to move the middle factors. Their product is the tower equation for $w_{FG}$ with the input and output tensor associators. Apply this first to $A$ and then to $\beta$, using the tower laws of [lem-pur-rational-normalized-purity-diagrams] and the scalar associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The intermediate associators cancel. Step 6 is a pasting of the same canonical tensor maps, hence is preserved under this substitution; Step 7 is a pasting of naturality and the single-purity squares, whose tower laws are already included in that node. For identity extensions each factor is the unit comparison, giving the identity boundary squares. For shifts substitute the shift laws of that node into Step 7; in Step 6 use the even-shift calculation of Step 5. This verifies the asserted identity, tower and shift identifications without an extra coherence assumption.
